title: GoldenTestCase
description: Self-contained regression-test bundle (§9.3, §9.4). A conforming runtime, driven by `fake_script` against `config + problem_statement`, MUST produce an `Artifact` whose `transcript_digest` (§7.7) equals `expected_artifact.transcript_digest`. This is the primary comparison rule. A stronger secondary assertion — full canonical_transcript byte equality after RFC-8785 JCS canonicalization — is RECOMMENDED. Comparison is byte-level on the JCS-canonical serialization, never on raw JSON formatting (§7.5, §7.7). Update workflow: when intended runtime behavior changes (a bug fix that alters output, a schema extension), the operator regenerates `expected_artifact` and commits the JCS-canonical diff for human review (§9.3). Byte-identity under JCS canonicalization is conditional on the §9.4.1 GoldenTestCase harness pinning requirements (deterministic message-id allocator + fixed-clock source). This is strictly weaker than the §7.6 production `execution_replay` pinning conditions (no provider, model, cache, or tool environment is involved) but stronger than the unconditional `transcript_replay` guarantee (golden tests *produce* a transcript rather than read one). The three contracts remain distinct (rule N12, §2.7 A2/N3 qualifier).

schema_version.description: Schema version per §5.1. The Pass 7 schema is `1.0.0`.

case_id.description: Stable identifier for the case. Same charset as `RunManifest.session_id` (§7.1) so a case_id can serve double-duty as a `session_id` when the harness writes the produced Artifact to disk under `runs/<case_id>/`.

description.description: Human-readable rationale for the case (what behavior it exercises, what regression it would catch).

problem_statement.description: The Originator's problem statement, forwarded verbatim to the runtime at session **init** (§4.1). Persisted into the canonical_transcript as the round-0 message.

config.description: Full Config object driving the run. MUST validate against `config.schema.json`. The harness MUST register the FakeProvider under whatever `provider` identifier the agents reference; the exact registration mechanism is implementation-defined (§6.11).

fake_script.description: Scripted FakeProvider responses driving the run (§9.1, §9.2).

expected_artifact.description: Expected Artifact at session end. MUST validate against `artifact.schema.json` AND satisfy the §7.7 semantic check (digest equals JCS-canonical SHA-256 of canonical_transcript; cumulative_usage equals message-level usage sum). The primary regression signal is `expected_artifact.transcript_digest`; the secondary signal is full canonical_transcript byte equality after JCS canonicalization.

expected_assertions.description: Optional list of scheduler-property assertions the case is designed to exercise. The harness MAY validate each named assertion alongside the primary digest comparison. The `category` enum partitions the §9.5–§9.9 catalogues; `name` identifies the specific invariant within a category (e.g. category=`scheduler_invariant`, name=`declared_order` for §4.10 invariant 2). Canonical names are listed in §9.5 / §9.6 / §9.7 / §9.8 / §9.9; the schema keeps `name` as an open string so future passes can extend the catalogue without a MAJOR bump.
